## Pooled normal equations

For this step all genotypes and seasons are pooled. The statistics are summed and the library columns scaled to unit root-mean-square, so that coefficients are comparable.


::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
st <- sum_years(gram, seq_along(tr$years))
A  <- apply(st$A, c(2, 3), sum)
b  <- colSums(st$b)
sc <- scale_gram(A, b, n = sum(st$n))
terms <- gram$names
```
:::


## Fitting methods

Each method takes `(A, b)` and returns `list(coef, support)`.

```r
fit_ols <- function(A, b, ...) {
  list(coef = solve(A, b), support = seq_along(b))
}
```

```r
fit_ridge <- function(A, b, lambda = 0.01, ...) {
  penalty <- lambda * mean(diag(A)) * diag(nrow(A))
  list(coef = solve(A + penalty, b), support = seq_along(b))
}
```

```r
fit_ssr <- function(A, b, k = 8, alpha = 1e-6, ...) {
  S <- seq_along(b)
  repeat {
    co <- solve(A[S, S, drop = FALSE] + alpha * diag(length(S)), b[S])
    if (length(S) <= k) break
    S <- S[-which.min(abs(co))]
  }
  coef <- numeric(length(b))
  coef[S] <- co
  list(coef = coef, support = S)
}
```


::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
fits <- list(OLS = fit_ols(sc$A, sc$b),
             ridge = fit_ridge(sc$A, sc$b, lambda = 0.01),
             SSR_8 = fit_ssr(sc$A, sc$b, k = 8))
coefs <- sapply(fits, `[[`, "coef")
rownames(coefs) <- terms
round(coefs, 3)
```

## Order of elimination

Sequential thresholding removes one term at a time; the order is the following.


::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
S <- seq_along(terms)
removed <- character(0)
while (length(S) > 1) {
  coef <- solve(sc$A[S, S] + 1e-6 * diag(length(S)), sc$b[S])
  drop <- which.min(abs(coef))
  removed <- c(removed, terms[S[drop]])
  S <- S[-drop]
}
c(removed, last = terms[S])
```

::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout}

```
                                                                                
"RAW^3" "RAD^3" "RAD^2"   "RAD"   "RAW"    "DL"  "TT^3"    "TT" "RAW^2"  "DL^3" 
                   last 
 "DL^2"  "TT^2"     "1" 
```


:::
:::


The order depends on the library and on correlations among its terms, and is not a ranking of importance. The number of terms is chosen by validation (step 5).

## Another method: lasso

Any method that maps `(A, b)` to coefficients can be used. As an example, the lasso by coordinate descent on the same scaled normal equations:

```r
fit_lasso <- function(A, b, lambda = 2e-4, iters = 2000, ...) {
  xi <- numeric(length(b))
  for (it in seq_len(iters)) {
    old <- xi
    for (j in seq_along(b)) {
      r <- b[j] - sum(A[j, -j] * xi[-j])
      xi[j] <- sign(r) * max(abs(r) - lambda, 0) / A[j, j]
    }
    if (max(abs(xi - old)) < 1e-9) break
  }
  list(coef = xi, support = which(xi != 0))
}
```


::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
las <- fit_lasso(sc$A, sc$b, lambda = 2e-4)
setNames(round(las$coef, 3), terms)
```
